titles_nl.11-08: Synaxis van Michaël en de onlichamelijke machten

summaries.01-01: On the eighth day the Child is circumcised and named Jesus. We also remember Basil the Great, archbishop of Caesarea: the liturgy that bears his name, the sobriety of fasting, the care for the poor.
summaries.01-02: The pope of Rome, and the elder who knelt in the snow.
summaries.01-03: The last prophet of the Old Covenant, and the soldier-martyr.
summaries.01-04: The seventy whom the Lord sent out, two by two.
summaries.01-05: The eve of Theophany. The Church fasts, reads the Royal Hours and prepares the water. Tomorrow the Jordan will turn back.
summaries.01-06: Christ goes down into the Jordan. The Father speaks, the Spirit descends like a dove. Not because He needs cleansing: He sanctifies the water, and with the water all creation. We bless the water and take it home.
summaries.01-07: The Forerunner, the greatest of those born of women.
summaries.01-08: The abbot by the Jordan, and the deaconess of Constantinople.
summaries.01-09: A soldier who sealed his baptism with his blood.
summaries.01-10: The theologian of the endless ascent to God.
summaries.01-11: Father of the common life in the desert of Judea.
summaries.01-12: Deaconess and martyr under Alexander Severus.
summaries.01-13: The deacon and the jailer, together in the Danube.
summaries.01-14: Monks slain in the desert; the close of Theophany.
summaries.01-15: The first hermit, and the son who lived in a hut beside his parents' house.
summaries.01-16: The chains of the prison in Jerusalem, a source of healing.
summaries.01-17: Anthony hears the Gospel in church, gives away his goods and goes into the desert. Athanasius wrote his life: the monk is the martyr of peace, and the struggle against the demons is fought in the open.
summaries.01-18: Two sees, one confession: the Son is true God.
summaries.01-20: The light of the desert of Palestine.
summaries.01-21: Two natures, two wills, one Christ. He lost his tongue, not the truth.
summaries.01-22: Paul's son in the faith, and the soldier who chose the cross.
summaries.01-23: A bishop and martyr from his youth.
summaries.01-24: The fool for Christ who took her husband's name and blessed the city.
summaries.01-25: The mouth of the Trinity, archbishop of Constantinople.
summaries.01-26: Father, mother, sons: one family, all the way to the monastery.
summaries.01-27: His relics return to the city that had exiled him.
summaries.01-28: The harp of the Spirit. The Lenten prayer is his.
summaries.01-29: The translation of the relics of the one who said: let me be food for the beasts.
summaries.01-30: The Church celebrated them separately until rivalry divided the faithful. Then they appeared together: we are one. Since then this day has been the feast of Orthodox theology and of Christian schools.
summaries.01-31: The unmercenary physicians, who healed without silver.
summaries.02-01: The wonderworker of the countryside, and the eve of Simeon.
summaries.02-02: Forty days after the Nativity, Mary brings the Child to the temple. Simeon and Anna, the old watchmen of Israel, recognise Him: a light to enlighten the Gentiles. The Mother of God hears of the sword that will pierce her soul.
summaries.02-03: The old man and the prophetess, the synaxis of the Meeting.
summaries.02-04: The abba of letters, sober and sharp.
summaries.02-06: A disciple of John, and the great patriarch Photius.
summaries.02-07: A bishop who drove out demons with gentleness.
summaries.02-08: The general who laid down his armour for the cross.
summaries.02-09: Martyr of friendship: he died in place of his enemy.
summaries.02-10: The aged priest-martyr whose relics still heal today.
summaries.02-11: Bishop and physician of people and animals.
summaries.02-12: The gentle bishop in the Arian storm.
summaries.02-13: The hermit who chose fire rather than temptation.
summaries.02-14: With Methodius he gave the Gospel an alphabet for the peoples of the north.
summaries.02-15: Philemon's slave, free in Christ, one of the Seventy.
summaries.02-17: The soldier of the kolyva, a foretaste of the fast.
summaries.02-18: The great pope of Chalcedon: two natures, unconfused and undivided.
summaries.02-20: The wonderworker who stood against the sorcerer Heliodorus.
summaries.02-22: Relics near Constantinople, a light beneath the earth.
summaries.02-23: Disciple of John. 'Eighty-six years I have served Him; how could I blaspheme Him now?'
summaries.02-24: The first and second finding of the head of John.
summaries.02-25: Patriarch of the Seventh Ecumenical Council, which restored the icons.
summaries.02-26: The bishop who brought down the idols of Gaza.
summaries.02-28: Companion of Procopius, steadfast in the struggle over the icons.
summaries.02-29: The bridge between Egypt and the West: the Conferences of the Fathers.
summaries.03-01: From sinner to martyr through a single word of a hermit.
summaries.03-02: A soldier who laid down his belt for Christ.
summaries.03-04: The abbot with the lion, father of the desert of Palestine.
summaries.03-05: A gardener and the apostle of his people.
summaries.03-06: Captives in the faith, unshaken until death.
summaries.03-09: Forty soldiers on a frozen lake, because they would not deny Christ. The warmth of the bathhouse lured one away; the guard saw the crowns and took his place. The Church sings of them in Lent as an icon of endurance.
summaries.03-10: Apostle of the Seventy, bishop and martyr.
summaries.03-11: Patriarch of the Holy City, who wrote the life of Mary of Egypt.
summaries.03-12: The chronicler of the icons, and the pope of the Dialogues.
summaries.03-13: Patriarch, exiled for the sake of the holy images.
summaries.03-14: Father of Western monasticism, honoured in the East.
summaries.03-17: The son who died as a beggar under the stairs of his parents' house.
summaries.03-18: The catecheses of the Holy City, the mysteries explained.
summaries.03-19: The married couple whose philosophy led them to martyrdom.
summaries.03-20: Slain in their monastery near Jerusalem.
summaries.03-21: A bishop who suffered for the icons.
summaries.03-23: One hundred and ninety-nine disciples with him.
summaries.03-24: Creation holds its breath. Zacharias the hermit.
summaries.03-25: In the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent. She answers: behold the handmaid of the Lord. No compulsion: the yes of one virgin is the door of the Incarnation. Today is the beginning of our salvation, the revelation of the eternal mystery.
summaries.03-26: The messenger of the Annunciation, and of all good news.
summaries.03-27: A servant girl, martyred by her mistress.
summaries.03-28: Abbot of Pelekete, a confessor of the icons.
summaries.03-30: John of Sinai, author of the Ladder. The Church reads him on the fourth Sunday of Lent: ascesis is not the goal, it is the ladder on which love climbs.
summaries.03-31: A bishop who died on the way back from Nicaea.
summaries.04-01: Seventeen years of sin, then the cross that held her back at the church door. The desert, Zosimas, and Communion carried across the Jordan. Her Sunday in Lent is the Church saying: no one is lost.
summaries.04-02: A monk of gentleness, working wonders without fuss.
summaries.04-03: A confessor of the holy icons.
summaries.04-04: The hymnographer of the Church, captive of pirates, free in song.
summaries.04-06: Patriarch, confessor of the two natures.
summaries.04-09: A martyr under Julian the Apostate.
summaries.04-11: The faithful witness of Revelation 2, in the furnace.
summaries.04-13: Pope of Rome, who died in exile for the two wills of Christ.
summaries.04-14: Of the Seventy, companions of Paul.
summaries.04-15: Aristarchus and his brothers in the Gospel.
summaries.04-16: Three sisters, the fire of Thessalonica.
summaries.04-17: Catholicos, martyred with hundreds of others.
summaries.04-19: A hermit near the Lavra of Chariton.
summaries.04-20: 'The hairy one', in a hair shirt until his death.
summaries.04-22: Wonderworker of Galatia, a bishop against his will.
summaries.04-23: George the Trophy-bearer. Not a fairy tale: a soldier who confesses Christ before the emperor. The Church honours him from Palestine to Russia. He is the knight of Pascha: the dragon underfoot, the maiden, the soul, set free.
summaries.04-24: A general and martyr under Aurelian.
summaries.04-25: The interpreter of Peter, the lion of Alexandria.
summaries.04-27: Second bishop of Jerusalem, crucified at the age of one hundred and twenty.
summaries.04-29: Of the Seventy, apostles of Corfu.
summaries.04-30: The first apostle to face the sword of Herod.
summaries.05-01: The weeping prophet, the covenant written on the heart.
summaries.05-02: The translation of his relics. Against the world, for the homoousios.
summaries.05-03: The young married couple, crucified together.
summaries.05-04: A bride of Christ, in the bronze bull.
summaries.05-06: The righteous man of Uz, an icon of Great Friday.
summaries.05-07: The cross of light above Golgotha in 351.
summaries.05-08: The beloved disciple, all the way to Ephesus. In the beginning was the Word.
summaries.05-09: The evangelist among the prophets, and the Christ-bearer.
summaries.05-10: The apostle of zeal, unto the cross.
summaries.05-11: Equal to the apostles, teachers of the Slavs.
summaries.05-12: The anchor of Orthodoxy, and the patriarch of the icons.
summaries.05-13: Martyr of Heraclea, before whom the stone gods fell.
summaries.05-15: Father of the common monastic life in Egypt.
summaries.05-16: Disciple of Pachomius and his second successor.
summaries.05-17: Of the Seventy, well known among the apostles.
summaries.05-18: An innkeeper and martyr, who saved the relics of the seven virgins.
summaries.05-19: A bishop-martyr in the hot springs.
summaries.05-21: Helena finds the true Cross. Constantine sees the sign in the sky. Not the glorification of power, but the conversion of power: the cross becomes the labarum, the city becomes New Rome.
summaries.05-22: Martyr of Comana, nephew of Theodore the Recruit.
summaries.05-24: A stylite, from his childhood on the pillar.
summaries.05-25: Again the head of John, a light in the darkness.
summaries.05-26: Bishop of Berea, companion of Paul.
summaries.05-27: A confessor in captivity, the saint of Euboea.
summaries.05-30: He stood against Valens the Arian at the city gate.
summaries.06-01: The apology to the emperor; the martyr of the Logos.
summaries.06-02: The translation of the relics of the patriarch and confessor.
summaries.06-03: The old priest of the idols, converted, with the child Paula.
summaries.06-04: First bishop of the city of Constantinople, under Constantine.
summaries.06-05: Bishop, martyred at the age of one hundred and seven.
summaries.06-06: The wonderworker of Egypt, and the abbot of Dalmatou.
summaries.06-09: Defender of the Mother of God at Ephesus. One incarnate Word.
summaries.06-10: The soldier and the virgin, together in the pit.
summaries.06-11: Two apostles, one day. The Israelite without guile, and the son of consolation.
summaries.06-12: The hermit clothed only in his hair, found by Paphnutius.
summaries.06-13: The obedient novice, obedient even after his death.
summaries.06-14: The double spirit of Elijah, and the patriarch of the icons.
summaries.06-15: The shepherd of Tekoa: let justice roll down like waters.
summaries.06-16: Bishop of Cyprus, the vine that bore fruit in winter.
summaries.06-19: The brother of the Lord, not the betrayer. Contend for the faith.
summaries.06-20: Bishop and martyr; on virginity and the resurrection.
summaries.06-21: A martyr thrown into the sea in a sack full of snakes.
summaries.06-22: Bishop and confessor against the Arians.
summaries.06-24: Six months before the Nativity of Christ, the barren woman gives birth. The greatest of those born of women, and yet the least in the Kingdom is greater than he, because he points to the Bridegroom and himself decreases.
summaries.06-26: The tree-hermit, three years in an almond tree.
summaries.06-27: Physician of Constantinople, the hostel for the poor.
summaries.06-28: The unmercenary physicians brought to Menouthis.
summaries.06-29: The fisher of men and the apostle of the Gentiles. Peter, who denied three times and loved three times; Paul, who persecuted and then laboured more than all. Together in Rome, together in the crown. The end of the Apostles' Fast.
summaries.06-30: The twelve thrones, the foundation of the Church.
summaries.07-01: The unmercenary physicians of the West.
summaries.07-02: Her veil (maphorion) in Blachernae, the protection of the city.
summaries.07-03: A chamberlain, starved to death because he would not sacrifice.
summaries.07-04: The Great Canon of Lent: repentance in two hundred and fifty troparia.
summaries.07-05: Founder of the Great Lavra, father of the Holy Mountain.
summaries.07-06: Before the bones of Alexander: death has stripped the king.
summaries.07-08: The great martyr, from persecutor to confessor.
summaries.07-09: Disciple of Peter, bishop-martyr of Sicily.
summaries.07-11: The Tome of Chalcedon was found in her hands in her tomb.
summaries.07-13: The archangel's second feast of the year.
summaries.07-14: With Priscilla: tentmakers, with a church in their house.
summaries.07-16: Bishop-martyr; the hymn of the evening light.
summaries.07-17: The great martyr who overcame the dragon of hell.
summaries.07-18: The young man who burned the idols.
summaries.07-19: Macrina, teacher of her brothers, the Cappadocians. And Seraphim: 'My joy, Christ is risen! Acquire the Spirit of peace, and thousands around you will be saved.'
summaries.07-20: Zeal for the Lord. Carmel, the brook Cherith, the widow of Zarephath, Horeb, the still small voice. He went up in fire. The Church honours him as the living one who stood with Moses on Tabor and who will come before the day of the Lord.
summaries.07-21: The fool for Christ and his companion in the desert.
summaries.07-22: Equal to the apostles. The first witness of the Resurrection.
summaries.07-24: The martyr, and the first passion-bearers of the Rus'.
summaries.07-25: The mother of the Mother of God, at the end of her days.
summaries.07-26: Panteleimon's priest, and the Friday martyr.
summaries.07-27: The great martyr and unmercenary physician.
summaries.07-30: Of the Seventy, companions of Paul.
summaries.07-31: The cross goes out; the righteous man of Cappadocia.
summaries.08-01: The Dormition Fast begins. The cross is carried out to ward off the sicknesses of August. The seven Maccabees, their mother Solomonia and the priest Eleazar: the Old Covenant dies as a martyr for the Law, an icon of Holy Week.
summaries.08-02: The first martyr, from Jerusalem to Constantinople.
summaries.08-03: The three abbots of the Dalmatou monastery.
summaries.08-04: The youths of the cave who awoke after centuries: the resurrection is no fable.
summaries.08-05: Tabor draws near. Eusignius the martyr.
summaries.08-06: He took Peter, James and John, and His face shone like the sun. With St Gregory Palamas the Church confesses that this light is not created but the energy of God, which the apostles saw for a moment. Moses and Elijah, the Law and the Prophets, speak of His departure in Jerusalem. We bless the fruits.
summaries.08-07: A converted magus, stoned in his cave.
summaries.08-08: Bishop and confessor of the icons.
summaries.08-09: The lot fell on him, in the place of Judas.
summaries.08-10: The deacon: 'Here are the treasures of the Church: the poor.'
summaries.08-11: Deacon-martyr, with the Gospel on his breast.
summaries.08-12: Uncle and nephew, in the furnace of Nicomedia.
summaries.08-13: The translation of his relics. The two wills of Christ.
summaries.08-14: The Mother of God approaches her departure. The prophet of Bethlehem.
summaries.08-15: She falls asleep. The apostles come on the clouds. Thomas comes late and finds only the grave clothes. No passing over without death: she goes before us in death and in life. Her Son is the Resurrection; her body sees no corruption.
summaries.08-16: The Mandylion of Edessa, the face of the Lord.
summaries.08-18: The stonemasons who turned a pagan temple into a church.
summaries.08-19: A general with 2,593 soldiers, all martyrs.
summaries.08-20: The seer, the anointing of David, the voice in the night.
summaries.08-21: The apostle of Edessa and the image of the Lord.
summaries.08-23: Servant of Demetrius, and the leave-taking of the Dormition.
summaries.08-24: Disciple of John, bishop of Sebaste.
summaries.08-25: The return of the relics, and the bishop of Crete.
summaries.08-26: The martyr couple: she strengthened him to the crown.
summaries.08-27: Abba of the Sayings: be silent, weep, do not judge.
summaries.08-28: From robber to abba: the power of repentance.
summaries.08-29: Herod, Herodias, the dance, the oath. John dies because he told the truth about an unlawful marriage. The Church fasts on this day. The Forerunner goes down to the dead to announce the Bridegroom there too.
summaries.08-31: Her belt in Chalkoprateia, for the healing of the empress.
summaries.09-01: The Church begins her year on 1 September, blessing the waters of time. Simeon stands on his pillar: man as a candle between heaven and earth. We pray for fruitfulness for the earth and peace for the cities.
summaries.09-02: The shepherd-boy martyr, and the patriarch of sobriety.
summaries.09-03: A bishop burned in the Great Persecution.
summaries.09-04: The patriarch who sent the emperor out of the church.
summaries.09-05: Father of the Forerunner, slain between the temple and the altar.
summaries.09-06: The archangel splits the rock, and the water turns aside.
summaries.09-07: Sozon the martyr. Tomorrow Anna gives birth.
summaries.09-08: Joachim and Anna, barren until old age. The child Mary is the gate of gates. The Church sings: today, grace, joy. From her the Word will become flesh; her birth is already Gospel.
summaries.09-09: The ancestors of God, parents of the Mother of God.
summaries.09-11: She lived in the monastery dressed as a man, until her death.
summaries.09-13: The centurion of Caesarea, firstfruits of the Gentiles.
summaries.09-14: Helena found it; the bishop raises it to the four winds and we bow down. Through the Cross joy has come into all the world. The Church fasts on this day: the wood is glory, but it remains the wood of Great Friday.
summaries.09-15: The Gothic martyr, burned in his house.
summaries.09-16: The great martyr, her second commemoration.
summaries.09-17: The mother and her three daughters: the theological virtues written in blood.
summaries.09-20: The general, the stag with the cross, and a whole family martyred.
summaries.09-21: Of the Seventy; the apology to Hadrian.
summaries.09-22: Gardener-bishop and martyr, protector of sailors.
summaries.09-23: Zechariah falls silent, Elizabeth conceives. The Forerunner is conceived.
summaries.09-24: The first woman martyr, disciple of Paul.
summaries.09-25: The virgin of Alexandria, and the abbot who blessed the Rus'.
summaries.09-26: The beloved disciple falls asleep at Ephesus. His tomb gave forth manna.
summaries.09-28: Founder of the lavras in the desert of Judea.
summaries.09-29: Of the Lavra of Chariton, until the age of one hundred and seven.
summaries.09-30: Apostle of Armenia, equal to the apostles.
summaries.10-01: In the church of Blachernae, Andrew the Fool sees her praying, spreading her veil over the people. The Mother of God is our protection, not an ornament. In the north this is one of the most beloved feasts: beneath your protection we take refuge.
summaries.10-02: The sorcerer converted by the virgin; martyrs together.
summaries.10-03: The judge of Athens, disciple of Paul, theologian of the hierarchies.
summaries.10-04: Companion of Dionysius, present at the Dormition.
summaries.10-06: 'My Lord and my God.' The hand in the side, the faith that came through doubt.
summaries.10-08: The actress of Antioch, a hermit on the Mount of Olives.
summaries.10-09: The apostle, not the brother of the Lord.
summaries.10-10: Brother and sister, martyrs of Nicomedia.
summaries.10-11: One of the seven: the Ethiopian official, Samaria.
summaries.10-13: Disciples of Paul, martyrs of Pergamum.
summaries.10-14: Four martyrs of Milan, and the patron saint of the Balkans.
summaries.10-15: Of Thessalonica, a hermit of Athos.
summaries.10-16: 'Truly this was the Son of God.' The spear, and faith beneath the cross.
summaries.10-17: 'I will heal their faithlessness'; the hymnographer-martyr.
summaries.10-18: The beloved physician, the icon of the Mother of God, the Acts of the Apostles.
summaries.10-19: 'I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh'; the hermit of Bulgaria.
summaries.10-20: The great martyr, governor of Egypt.
summaries.10-21: Disciple of Anthony, father of the monks of Palestine.
summaries.10-22: Equal to the apostles; the epitaph of the mystery of the fish.
summaries.10-23: First bishop of Jerusalem: the liturgy and the letter.
summaries.10-24: The martyr of Arabia, with his city.
summaries.10-25: Notaries of Constantinople, martyrs for the homoousios.
summaries.10-26: The soldier of Thessalonica. Nestor defeats the gladiator in the name of the God of Demetrius, and both die. His myrrh flows to this day. The Church honours him with George as a great soldier-saint of the East.
summaries.10-27: The disciple of Demetrius, victorious in the arena.
summaries.10-28: The martyr family, and the Friday saint of Asia Minor.
summaries.10-30: Brother and sister, physicians, martyrs of Cilicia.
summaries.10-31: Of the Seventy, apostles of Byzantium.
summaries.11-01: The unmercenary physicians, sons of Theodota.
summaries.11-02: Five martyrs of Persia under Shapur.
summaries.11-03: A bishop, a priest and a deacon of Persia.
summaries.11-04: A soldier, then a hermit of Mount Olympus in Bithynia.
summaries.11-05: The couple of Emesa, living in virginity, martyred together.
summaries.11-06: Patriarch of Constantinople, strangled for the homoousios.
summaries.11-08: The Church honours the bodiless powers. Michael, who cast down the dragon; Gabriel, the messenger; Raphael, the healer. The liturgy on earth is an icon of the liturgy in heaven. We are not alone.
summaries.11-09: The abbess of Constantinople, and the gentle bishop of our times.
summaries.11-10: Of the Seventy, named in Romans 16.
summaries.11-11: The great martyr of Egypt, with his companions.
summaries.11-12: Patriarch of Alexandria: almsgiving as liturgy.
summaries.11-13: Archbishop of Constantinople, exiled for the truth. The Church prays his Liturgy most of the year. He preached Scripture verse by verse; for him the rich man and Lazarus was not just a parable but a judgement on the city.
summaries.11-14: 'Come and see.' The apostle of Bethsaida; the beginning of the Nativity Fast.
summaries.11-15: Martyrs of Edessa. The beginning of the Nativity Fast.
summaries.11-16: The tax collector, the first Gospel, the Child and the Magi.
summaries.11-17: Of Neocaesarea. The Creed received in a vision of John and the Mother of God.
summaries.11-19: The vision about Edom; the day of the Lord.
summaries.11-20: Mary draws near the temple. The confessor of the icons.
summaries.11-21: Joachim and Anna bring her. The high priest leads her behind the veil, where no one was allowed. She herself is the Holy of Holies, the living ark. Here the Church already senses Christmas: the temple receives the dwelling place of God.
summaries.11-22: Paul's letter, the slave Onesimus, the church in his house.
summaries.11-23: Bishop of Iconium, friend of Basil; and the bishop of Sicily.
summaries.11-24: The third successor of Peter, and the martyr-patriarch who wrote on the lapsed.
summaries.11-25: The philosopher of the wheel, and the soldier of Caesarea.
summaries.11-26: Sixty-seven years on his pillar near Adrianople.
summaries.11-27: Cut in pieces, limb by limb, to the crown.
summaries.11-28: The great martyr of the icons, under Constantine Copronymus.
summaries.11-30: The first disciple, apostle of Byzantium, the diagonal cross.
summaries.12-01: Nineveh, the city of blood. The Lord is a stronghold.
summaries.12-02: The righteous shall live by his faith. The watchman on the tower.
summaries.12-03: The day of the Lord, the remnant of Israel.
summaries.12-04: Barbara, locked up by her father, confesses the Trinity with three windows. John of Damascus, monk of St Sabbas: the icon is possible because the Word became flesh. Against the emperor, for the Face.
summaries.12-05: Father of the great lavra, the typikon of Palestine.
summaries.12-06: Bishop of Myra in Lycia. He strikes Arius out of zeal, not anger; he saves the three generals, the three girls and the sailors. East and West honour him as the icon of the shepherd: hidden almsgiving, open confession.
summaries.12-07: The governor who became bishop. Theodosius had to bow.
summaries.12-08: A hermit near Constantinople, a healer.
summaries.12-09: Anna conceives Mary. The yes of the parents, before the yes of the Virgin.
summaries.12-11: The pillar saint on the Bosphorus, counsellor of emperors.
summaries.12-12: Spyridon at Nicaea: the Trinity is not arithmetic. The brick in his hand becomes three that are one. He remains the village shepherd in his wicker hat, a wonderworker to this day.
summaries.12-13: The five martyrs of Armenia, the wise Eustratius.
summaries.12-15: The young bishop-martyr, with his mother Anthia.
summaries.12-16: 'Build this house, and I will take pleasure in it.'
summaries.12-17: The fiery furnace, the lions' den, the Son of Man.
summaries.12-18: The soldier at the stake, the arrows, the second death.
summaries.12-19: From Rome to the East for relics, and became a relic himself.
summaries.12-20: The bishop of Antioch, disciple of John. On the way to Rome he wrote seven letters: the Eucharist is the medicine of immortality, the bishop an icon of the Father. He died in the arena. The Church already senses the manger.
summaries.12-21: Virgin-martyr, who overcame the devil in prison.
summaries.12-22: The Roman healer of prisoners, a martyr.
summaries.12-23: Under Decius, the island turned to blood.
summaries.12-24: The eve. The Church holds her breath: the cave of Bethlehem, the Magi on the way, the shepherds in the night. Tomorrow, the Word.
summaries.12-25: Bethlehem. The cave, the manger, the Mother of God, Joseph the guardian, the angels, the shepherds, the Magi. Not a children's story: the Incarnation of the second Person of the Trinity. He becomes poor so that we may become rich. The Sun of righteousness rises. Christ is born, glorify Him!
summaries.12-26: The day after the Nativity belongs to her who gave birth without corruption.
summaries.12-27: 'Behold, I see the heavens opened.' The first martyr.
summaries.12-28: Burned in their church on the feast of Christ's birth.
summaries.12-29: The Holy Innocents, the first martyrs of the New Covenant.
summaries.12-30: A virgin-martyr on her way to the liturgy.
summaries.12-31: The leave-taking of the Nativity, and the Roman woman who gave everything away.
